title: Home beer dispenser (multi-agent)
description: a home beer dispenser designed to dispense bottled beer using a hand-operated valve and compressed carbon dioxide
reference_excerpt: The product in question is a home beer dispenser, specifically designed for dispensing bottled beer. It operates using a hand-operated valve that introduces compressed carbon dioxide (CO2) into the beer bottle, pressurizing it to control the flow of beer. The dispenser is made from various plastic components. According to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), the applicable subheading for this type of product falls under 8481.80.5090, which covers "other taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, hand operated, of other materials." The classification is appropriate because the product is primarily a hand-operated valve mechanism used for dispensing, fitting the descri.

text: {"heading":"8481","best_code":"8481.80.50.90","argument":"Heading 8481 covers 'Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like, including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves; parts thereof.' The valve mechanism is the essential functional component that defines the article. The product falls within 8481.80 (Other appliances) as a hand-operated valve appliance. Under GRI 6, subheading 8481.80.50 applies to hand-operated appliances of other materials (metal and plastic components). memo.argument: Heading 8481 covers 'Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like, including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves; parts thereof.' The home beer dispenser is a complete assembled appliance with an integrated hand-operated valve that controls the flow of bottled beer using compressed CO2 pressure. The valve mechanism is the essential functional component that defines the article. The product falls within 8481.80 (Other appliances) as a hand-operated valve appliance. Under GRI 6, subheading 8481.80.50 applies to hand-operated appliances of other materials (metal and plastic components). The 10-digit code 8481.80.50.90 (Other) is the appropriate statistical line for a home beer dispenser that does not fit the specific categories of pressure spray can valves or bath/shower/sink faucets.
exclusions_against: Chapter 84 note 1(f) excludes 'Electromechanical domestic appliances of heading 8509' but this product is hand-operated, not electromechanical, so the exclusion does not apply.
Section XVI note 1 does not contain exclusions that would remove valve appliances from Chapter 84 coverage.

text: {"heading":"8210","best_code":"8210.00.00.00","argument":"Heading 8210 covers 'Hand-operated mechanical appliances, weighing 10 kg or less, used in the preparation, conditioning or serving of food or drink, and base metal parts thereof.' The beer dispenser is a hand-operated mechanical appliance (controlled by a hand-operated valve) designed specifically for serving beverages (beer). It is complete and assembled, weighs under 10 kg, and consists of metal and plastic components. The product directly fits the statutory language of heading 8210 as an appliance used in the serving of drink. Ruling R01157 (in force, 2004) classified a drink dispenser under 8210.00.0000 on identical reasoning. The product is not excluded by Chapter 82 notes, which apply only to articles with blades, working edges, or cutting surfaces—none of which this dispenser possesses.","supporting_rulings":[{"id":"R01157","status":"in_force"}],"exclusions_against":["Chapter 82 Note 1 excludes articles without a blade, working edge, working surface or other working part of base metal, metal carbides, or abrasive materials—but this exclusion does not apply to heading 8210, which is carved out as an exception ('apart from...goods of heading 8209, this chapter covers only...')"],"strength":0.85}

memo.argument: Heading 8210 covers 'Hand-operated mechanical appliances, weighing 10 kg or less, used in the preparation, conditioning or serving of food or drink, and base metal parts thereof.' The beer dispenser is a hand-operated mechanical appliance (controlled by a hand-operated valve) designed specifically for serving beverages (beer). It is complete and assembled, weighs under 10 kg, and consists of metal and plastic components. The product directly fits the statutory language of heading 8210 as an appliance used in the serving of drink. Ruling R01157 (in force, 2004) classified a drink dispenser under 8210.00.0000 on identical reasoning. The product is not excluded by Chapter 82 notes, which apply only to articles with blades, working edges, or cutting surfaces—none of which this dispenser possesses.
exclusions_against: Chapter 82 Note 1 excludes articles without a blade, working edge, working surface or other working part of base metal, metal carbides, or abrasive materials—but this exclusion does not apply to heading 8210, which is carved out as an exception ('apart from...goods of heading 8209, this chapter covers only...')

memo.argument: Heading 3924 covers 'Tableware, kitchenware, other household articles and hygienic or toilet articles, of plastics.' A home beer dispenser is a household article made of plastic and metal components designed for home beverage service. The product functions as a dispensing appliance for domestic use, similar to other household beverage service items. Chapter 39 note 2(s) excludes 'Articles of section XVI (machines and mechanical or electrical appliances),' but this product is hand-operated and not primarily a machine or mechanical appliance in the sense of Chapter 84 machinery. The dispenser is fundamentally a household article for serving beverages at home, making it classifiable under heading 3924 as 'other household articles' of plastics rather than as industrial machinery.
exclusions_against: Chapter 39 note 2(s) excludes articles of Section XVI (machinery and mechanical appliances); a hand-operated valve-based dispenser with CO2 regulator may be argued to fall within heading 8481 (taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances) as demonstrated by ruling H250151 classifying a similar wine dispenser in 8481.80.50
Chapter 39 note 2(m) excludes containers of heading 4202, but this is an integrated dispenser, not a container

Revoked rulings N016275 and L89010 previously classified similar plastic dispensers with hand-operated valves in 3926.90 (other articles of plastics), suggesting the product may not fit squarely in 3924 tableware/kitchenware subcategories
